lawyer:
Shasti Sarker, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
Md Nurul Amin, Advocate ------ For the Opposite-Party. Nos. 1-3.
parties:
Puspa Rani Chowdhury ------ Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner
Vs.
Md Emdad Hossain and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 22-1-2008 passed by the learned Special District Judge, Kushtia in Title Appeal No. 140 of 2005 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30-6-2005 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Kushtia in Title Suit No. 92 of 1993 in decreeing the suit for specific performance of contract.

2. It may be noted that this revisional application was filed with a delay of 140 days and in that respect Civil Rule No. 583(Con) of 2008 was issued and subsequently the rule was made absolute by order of this court dated 17-2-2009.

3. The opposite-party Nos. 1-3 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.92 of 1993 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Kumarkhali, Kushtia impleading the present petitioner as defendant No.1 and others praying for a decree for specific performance of contract.

4. The plaintiff case, in short are that the suit land morefully described in the schedule of the plaint is under Mouza Damdama and Bagulat, Police Station-Kumarkhali, District Kushtia belongs to defendant No.1 Srimati Bhabani Bala. The defendant No.2 proposed to sell the land due to met funeral expenses and to pay the loan of her deceased husband. The defendant No.1 proposed to sell land and plaintiffs were agreed to purchase the same for a total consideration of Taka 1,65,000 and accordingly a bainanama was executed on receipt of Taka 1,25,000 on 27-1-1993. It was stipulated therein that on payment of balance consideration of Taka 40,000, the defendant will execute and register the sale deed. The plaintiffs requested to receive the rest of the money but in spite of repeated demand defendant did not execute and register the kabala and last demand was made on 1-8-1993 but she refused to register the suit land and hence the suit.

5. The defendant Nos.1 and 2 contested the said suit by filing a separate written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and also barred under the principles of waiver, estoppel. There is no cause of action of the suit and the plaintiff’s present suit is not maintainable under sections 39 and 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The positive case of defendant No.1 is that she sold some portion of land for repayment of loan of her deceased husband and also to met funeral expenses. At that time the plaintiffs purchased some non suited land on 3-3-1993 by two registered deed Nos. 272 and 1273 and also by another deed No.4370 dated 17-7-1993. The defendant No.1 had no such requirement to sell the aforesaid land there is no question to purchase the further land. At the time of execution and registration of the aforesaid deeds the plaintiffs took some signature of the defendant No. 1 in the some blank stamp papers and subsequently created those papers as the alleged binanama 27-1-1993. The defendant never sell the land in favour of the plaintiff and she never executed such bainanama in favour of the plaintiff after receipt of total consideration money Taka 1,65,000 and never delivered possession in favour of the plaintiff. It was further stated that the plaintiffs did not disclose about the said bainanama before filing of the suit. Even he did not serve any notice in accordance with the provision of law. The plaintiffs however instituted the present suit by converting the said blank papers into an alleged bainanama. With these averments, the defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit.

6. The defendant No. 3, Md Abul Hossain Mollah, subsequent purchaser from defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing separate written statement. The positive case of the defendant is that the area of land measuring '25 acres of SA Khatian No. 96 of Kalikatola Mouza belong's to defendant No. 1. Area of '26 acres under S.A. Khatian No. 14 of Bagulat Mouza, '21 acres of land from Plot No. 834, '09 acres of land from Plot No. 460, '25 acres of land from Plot No. 834 of Mouza Damdama Mouza, '25 acres of land from Plot No. 174 of Mouza Kalikatola in total 1.09 acres belongs to defendant No.1. She entered into an bainanama on 15-12-1992 for sale of the suit land for a total consideration of Taka 78,000 out of which the defendant No.3 paid Taka 50,000 as advance and delivered possession to defendant No. 3. Subsequently, defendant No.1 further received a sum of Taka 10,000 on 2-2-1993, Taka 8,000 on 3-3-1993, and Taka 7,000 on 4-4-1993 by putting her signature on the back side of the bainanama. Latter on he did not execute and register the Kabala after receiving the balance amount of Taka 3,000. The defendant No. 1 refused to register the kabala on 2-2-1994, then he filed a Title Suit No. 31 of 1994 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kumarkhali impleading the defendant No.1 as defendant and got a decree on 22-8-1994 and after decree defendant No.1 withdraw Taka 3,000 deposited in the said suit. This defendant filed Title Execution case being No. 4 of 1994 and got a registered Kabala No.1032 dated 26-2-1995 through court and took possession on 3-12-1995. Subsequently, this defendant mutated the land through Mutation Case No. 532/9-2/94-95. The present plaintiff and one Abu Taleb Sk. filed Title Suit No. 56 of 1995 impleading present defendant as defendant No.1 and Bhabani Bala Chowdhury as defendant No.2 and prayed for a declaration that the Judgment and decree dated 22-8-1994 passed in Title Suit No. 31 of 1994 is illegal, collusive, inoperative, void and the deed is not binding upon the plaintiff. In that suit, the present defendant No.2, Bhabani Bala Chowdhury filed written statement and admits the bainanama dated 15-12-1992 and the Title Suit No. 31 of 1994 which is filed in respect of bainanama dated 15-12-1992. This defendant and Bhabani Bala Chowdhury contested in Title Suit No.56 of 1995 and the learned court was pleased to dismiss the suit on 24-6-1997. The plaintiffs have no right, title, interest in the suit land; that the land measuring 26 acres in schedule-1 and 0.58 acres of land described in scheduled-2 and the rest land have been in possession of the defendant No.1 for more than twelve years. The defendant No. 1 disclosed on 14th Magh, 1399 BS correspondence on 27-1-1993 that she did not execute any bainanama in favour of the plaintiff. That the plaintiff is aware about the bainanama executed between the defendant No. 3 and plaintiff. The plaintiff has filed this case just to harass the defendant. Hence, this defendant prays for dismissal of the suit.

7. In this suit plaintiff adduced four p.ws and defendant examined five P.ws to prove their respective case. The learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Kushtia after considering evidence and materials on record decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 13-6-2005.

8. Against the aforesaid judgment of the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Kushtia, the defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No. 140 of 2005 and defendant No.3 also preferred Title Appeal No.158 of 2005 before the learned District Judge, Kushtia. Eventually, on transfer both the appeals were heard analogously by the Special Judge, Kushtia, who by a single judgment dismissed both the appeal by judgment and decree dated 22-1-2008.

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 22-1-2008 passed by the learned Special Judge, Kushtia, the defendant No.1 moved this revisional application and obtained the present Rule.

10. Mr Shasti Sarker, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioner submits that since the defendant denied the execution of the bainanama dated 27-1-1993 but the plaintiff by adducing any evidence failed to prove the bainanama, the appellate court has committed gross an error of law is not dismissing the suit. He further submits that both the courts below committed gross error of law in considering the report of the hand writing expert and that said report ought to have been cancelled because of the fact that the thumb impressions of bainanama are not the thumb impressions of defendant No. 1 He next submits that in a suit for specific performance of contract when the executant deny the execution of the bainapatra it is the duty of the plaintiff to prove the genuineness by comparing the signature with the admitted signature but in the present case same has not been done. He also submits that the scribe of the deed was not examined in the present case rather he was withdrawn as such the defendant will get advantage under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. He further submits that the bainanama has been created by his obedient person who clearly appears that one thumb impressions over stamp papers on the right side and another one on the left side of the demi papers. He finally submits that the appellate court committed gross error of law in misreading, misconstruing, miss appreciating and non-consider the materials and evidence on record. In support of his submission, he cited certain decisions specially on the point of expert opinion reported in 50 DLR (AD) 88, 45 DLR 169, 1 BLC (AD) 85. It may be noted here that in support of his submission on the finger-print of the defendant No.1, he referred the Book "Disputed Documents Examination and Finger-prints Identification by HR Hardless", 5th Edition 1997, regarding the identity of the LTI in respect of 16 ridge characteristics. He also referred a decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) (1987) 156 in respect of onus on whom lies in a suit for specific performance of contract for sale of the property where the signatures in the documents recording the contract is admitted by the defendants pleading that the same was obtained by threat, intimidation and coercion.

11. On the other hand, Mr Md Nurul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs-opposite-parties by referring paragraph 8 of the written statement submits that since the defendant No.1 has made out an alternative case and denied the execution of the bainanama dated 27-1-1997 stating that: অন্য দলিল Execute করার সময় Black Stamp Paper's sign করে নেয়। In refuting the argument of the learned Advocate of the petitioner, he submits that whether the bainapatra is genuine one or not as the same is denied by the defendant No.1, it is solemn duty of the defendant to prove the said fact that at the time of bainanama some signatures /LTI were obtained by the plaintiff. In support of his submission Mr Md Nurul Amin relied upon the decisions reported in 42 DLR 344, 7 BLD (AD) (1997) 156 = 2 BLC (AD) 103 (which was also relied by the learned Advocate for the petitioner). He next submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the defendant failed to prove that no bainanama was executed in favour of the plaintiff on 27-1-1993 and both the courts below after considering the evidence of attesting witnesses PW 3 and PW 4 in respect of execution and payment of money proved the bainanama. On the contrary, the P.ws failed to prove the alternative story of obtaining LTI malafidely by the plaintiff on the so called bainanama. On this point the learned Advocate relied on the decisions reported in 64 DLR (AD) 133 and 17 BLD (AD) 199 = 2 BLC (AD) 134. He also submits that the defendant No.1 as d.w.1 failed to prove the alternative story stating in her pleadings but in the deposition he categorically stated that: বায়নার কথা জানি না DW 2 did not corroborate such fact.

12. Learned Advocate further submits that the decision which was referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner reported in 2 BLC (AD) 285 has no manner of application in the present case because of the fact that the expert opinion must be considered with other materials on record and should not be considered expert opinion alone but in the preset case courts below considered expert opinion along with other evidence and materials on record. Mr Md Nurual Amin by referring the order sheet of the trial court specially order dated 13-10-2004 submits that the hand writing expert, court witness, SK Mostafizur Rahman submitted report dated 23.07.1998 but no objection was filed against the said report which will be clearly reveal from order No.51 dated 13-4-2004 but objection was raised when the suit was fixed for pronouncement of the judgment. So, the defendant being a indolent person, he should not get benefit for his own default/wrong, who slept over his own right. He finally submits that both the courts below after considering the evidence and materials on record clearly found that the bainaparta was genuine one. The PWs.1-4 specially PW 3, the attesting witness of the bainapatra clearly stated that: Baina পাঠ করে শোনানো হয় and PW 4 also corroborated by PW 2 and PW 3 in respect of execution and payment of consideration money. In this respect learned Advocate referred the case of Md Fazlul Haque vs BM Rahman @ Mahbubur Rahman reported in 1 MLR (AD) 418. In the said decision it has been held that whether the bainapatra upon which the plaintiff was relying was genuine or not was a question of fact and the learned Additional District Judge upon a proper consideration of the evidence on record including the bainapatra found the case of the plaintiff to be unacceptable. This being a finding of fact, the High Court Division rightly refused to interfere with the same in revision.

13. In the present suit the plaintiff was able to prove the bainanama dated 27-1-1993 executed by the defendant No.1 in favour of the present plaintiffs by his witness Emdad, Firoz and Johir Uddin. Since the LTI of the bainanama was challenged by the defendant and same was sent to the hand writing expert for examination and the hand written expert as court witness proved the report Exhibit-8 dated 7-8-1998 that LTI and bainanama with the admitted LTI of the defendant No.1 Bhabani Bala in sale deed No.1272 dated 3-3-1993 Exhibit-l (Ka) and sale deed No.4371 dated 17-7-1993 Exhibit-1(Kha) respectively. In this respect Mr Shasti Sharker tried to submit that since the bainanama was executed by Bhabani Bala being পর্দানশীল লেডী, the same was not proved in accordance with law. In support of this submission, he referred a decision reported in 50 DLR (AD) 80.

14. I have gone through the decision reported in 50 DLR (AD) 80 but the facts and circumstances of the cited case are totally different from the facts and circumstances of the present case. In the present case the plaintiff was able to prove the Bainanama dated 27-1-1993 (Exhibit-1) by oral and documentary evidence and specially by Exhibit-X, Exhibts-1(Ka)- 1(Kha) and l(Gha).

15. In this connection learned Advocate for the opposite-party by referring section 103 of the Evidence Act tried to submits that burden of prove as to the alternative story stated by the defendant No. 1 in the present case to the effect that at the time of execution of kabalas Exhibt-1(Ka)- 1(Gha), plaintiff obtained LTI from the defendant No. 1 in some blank stamp papers. Since the defendant has failed to prove the said particular fact in the present case of specific performance contract. In the present suit the court after obtaining some LTI of defendant No.1 and comparing that LTI with the LTI appearing the Exhibit-1(Ka)-1(Gha) and also the LTI of bainanama dated 27-1-1993 (Exhibit- 1) clearly found that the LTI appearing in the bainanama and other are admitted LTI of the defendant No.1 are same/similar. In this respect reliance may be placed in a case of Chand Mia (Md) vs Khodeza Bibi reported in 42 DLR 344 wherein it has been held: Burden of proof as to particular fact the defendant in a suit for specific performance contract admits her LTI in the agreement for sale and offers an alternative story as to how her LTI came to be put on the document. The onus lies on her to prove the alternative story.

16. In the present case plaintiff has produced the bainanama as Exhibit-1 from the rightful custody and the defendant No.1 has admitted her LTI therein. She has however given an alternative story as to how she came to put her LTI in alleged bainaparta. But the courts below clearly found that the defendant No.1 failed to prove her alternative story and primary onus has been satisfactorily discharged by the plaintiff as to the execution of the bainanama (Exhibit-1). In this regard, reference may be made to the case of Jahed Ali Mondal vs Jamini Kanta Dey reported in 7 BLD (1987) (AD) 156 it has been held: Onus-Onus on whom lies in a suit for specific performance of a contract for sale of property where the signatures in the documents recording the contract is admitted by the defendant pleading that the same were obtained from them by threat, intimidation and coersion-Law does not require that all facts alleged by the plaintiff shall be strictly proved, for burden of proof is often lightened by presumptions, admissions and estoppels-Primarily onus of course lies, in a civil proceedings, upon the plaintiff-In this case primary onus has been discharged satisfactorily by the plaintiff. Then onus has shifted upon the defendants to prove their particular fact that their signatures were extorted. This onus they failed to discharge. Consequently, the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs as to the execution of the documents stands.

17. In the present case primary onus has been discharged satisfactorily by the plaintiff. Then onus has shifted upon the defendant to prove the particular fact that her LTI/signature was extorted but the defendant failed to discharge her onus. Consequently, the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs as to the execution documents stands. Since both the courts below have concurrently found that the bainanama was executed by the defendant No.1 and such concurrent findings of fact are immune from the interference by this revisional court and the learned Advocate for the petitioner failed to pin point anything that the trial court, as well as of the appellate court misread or non-considered any material evidence on record. In this connection, I can place reliance on the case of Habibur Rahman Bhuiyan (Md) vs Galman Begum reported in 64 DLR (AD) 133 where in our apex court held under: "When a finding of fact is based on consideration of the materials on record, those findings are immune from interference by the revisional Court except there is non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence on record. The High Court Division has no jurisdiction to sit on appeal over a finding of fact."

18. In this respect we can also rely on the case of Amanatullah vs Ali Mohammad Bhuiyan reported in 17 BLD (AD) (1997) 199 = 2 BLC (AD) 134 in that decision it has been held: "A finding of fact whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate Court is binding upon the High Court Division in revision except in certain well-defined circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case."

19. I have gone through the decision of both the courts below although the learned Advocate was trying to submit that there was misreading and non-consideration of material evidence but he was miserably failed to point out any misreading and non-consideration of any materials evidence on record.

<u>20. Let us now consider the decision referred by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The decision reported in 45 DLR 169 it was held that Examination of LTI—: It is true court itself can compare any signature or LTI of any concern person himself under section 73 of the Evidence Act, but it is better to have an expert's opinion also particularly in case of LTI. In the present case it appears that the expert opinion in respect of LTI of defendant No.1 in bainanama (Exhibit-1) and others admitted documents, Sale Deeds, Exhibits-I (Kha) - I (Gha) and Exhibit-X without given any objection from the defendant side. And it further appears that expert opinion (Exhibit-X) was submitted on 23-7-1998 and same was accepted. Against the said report of the hand writing expert no objection was raised by the defendant till 30-10-2004, when the suit was fixed for delivery of judgment. So, the decision of 45 DLR 169 will not any way help the learned Advocate for the petitioner. Learned Advocate for the petitioner also refers the case of 50 DLR (AD) 88 and 1 BLC (AD) 85 but citations as referred by the learned advocate for the petitioner has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case. Here in the instant case of the learned Advocate for the petitioner failed to point out that the impugned order has occasioned failure of justice to the present petitioner. The mere error of law without occasioning failure of justice cannot by itself be a ground for interference by this court under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and in that view of the matter I find nothing to interfere with the same.</u>

21. Thus having regard to all aspects of the case and on careful and overall consideration of the entire evidence on record, provisions of law and the decisions cited above, I am of the opinion that the concurrent findings of the courts below should not be interfered with.

22. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

Send down the lower court records expeditiously with a copy of judgment for information.

End.
